title: Nucleic Acid Extraction from FFPE Tissue
author: NCI Biorepositories and Biospecimen Research Branch
materials: Clean work area and metal equipment including microtome with a xylene-free deparaffinization reagent (See Section 8.3.2 in the Attached PDF for Expert Recommendations).
Wipe down all equipment, work area and all tools with RNase removal wipes or spray.

steps.title: Prepare Paraffin Blocks
steps.instruction: Prepare the paraffin blocks for sectioning by cooling them.

substeps.instruction: Place paraffin blocks face-down on a cold plate for at least 5 minutes, or at room temperature if blocks were stored at -20°C.

steps.title: Section FFPE Tissue
steps.instruction: Cut tissue sections using a microtome.

substeps.instruction: Use a new microtome blade for each biospecimen.
Position the FFPE tissue block in the specimen clamp of the microtome.
Cut sections 5-10 μm thick and allow them to roll up naturally.
Discard the first 3-4 sections.
Using RNase-free forceps, place the required number of sections (e.g., 1-8 sections for a 250 mm2 tissue surface area) directly into a sterile RNase-free microfuge tube.

steps.title: Deparaffinize Sections
steps.instruction: Remove paraffin from the tissue sections using xylene or an approved alternative.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 ml of xylene to the microcentrifuge tube or slide.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge tubes for 2 minutes at maximum speed (approximately 16,000-20,000 x g).
Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash and Dry Pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the tissue pellet to remove residual solvents and dry completely.

substeps.instruction: Wash the pellet/slide in 100% ethanol, vortex, and centrifuge at maximum speed at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Perform a second ethanol wash if necessary for low-quality specimens or specific deparaffinization techniques.
Ensure the pellet is completely dry by air-drying at room temperature or using a speed vacuum.

steps.title: Digest Tissue
steps.instruction: Perform enzymatic digestion of the tissue using lysis buffer and proteinase K.

substeps.instruction: Add lysis buffer containing proteinase K at the volume and concentration specified by the extraction kit.
Incubate at 55-56°C for 2-48 hours for DNA extraction, or for 15 minutes to overnight for RNA extraction.

steps.title: Demodify Nucleic Acids
steps.instruction: Heat the samples to demodify the nucleic acids (this step may be omitted depending on the analysis).

substeps.instruction: For DNA extraction: Heat tubes to 90°C for 10 minutes to 2 hours.
For RNA extraction: Heat tubes to 80°C for 0-15 minutes.

steps.title: Extract Nucleic Acids
steps.instruction: Perform the final extraction using an experimentally validated kit.

substeps.instruction: Follow the method specified by the extraction kit.
For DNA: Use silica, magnetic-bead, heating, resin-filter, ultrasonication, or salting-out methods (avoid organic extraction).
For RNA: Use silica, magnetic bead, organic, ultrasonication, or salting-out methods (avoid resin filter and heat-based methods).

steps.title: Purify Nucleic Acids
steps.instruction: Remove contaminating nucleic acids from the final extract.

substeps.instruction: Perform RNase treatment for DNA extracts or DNase treatment for RNA extracts (advised but not required).

steps.title: Quantify and Verify Quality
steps.instruction: Assess the yield and integrity of the extracted DNA and RNA.

substeps.instruction: Quantify DNA and RNA using a fluorometric or qPCR-based method.
Verify DNA integrity using fit-for-purpose quality metrics.

Verify RNA quality using the percentage of RNA fragments >200 nt (DV200) and/or a combination of DV200 and real-time qRT-PCR amplification of products from the 5’ and 3’ end of the transcript (avoid RIN).
